name: Lying Dumbbell Leg Curl
description: The lying dumbbell leg curl is performed face-down on a bench or the floor, with a dumbbell clamped between the feet. The lifter curls the dumbbell upward by bending the knees, isolating the hamstrings. It requires no machine and provides a practical home-gym alternative to the lying leg curl machine. Foot stability and control of the dumbbell demand additional concentration.

execution.starting_position: Lie face-down on a flat bench. Hold a dumbbell vertically between the soles of your feet, clamped firmly. Legs extended.
execution.setup_instructions: Choose a dumbbell you can hold securely between your feet. Lie prone on the bench with hips at the edge and legs hanging off.
steps: Step 1: Squeeze the dumbbell securely between both feet.
Step 2: Curl the dumbbell upward by bending the knees, bringing heels toward the glutes.
Step 3: Curl as far as knee flexion allows — ideally past 90 degrees.
Step 4: Lower the dumbbell slowly back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the controlled lowering.
common_mistakes: Dumbbell slipping or rotating — use a secure grip with both feet
Hips rising off the bench during the curl
Using momentum to swing the dumbbell up
safety_considerations: Ensure the dumbbell is firmly secured before each rep
Start light until foot clamping feels natural
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Curl from full extension to as much flexion as possible.
coaching_cues: Lead with the heels toward the glutes
